churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, configuration and typing are well isolated, so a framework or API-data change touches few files; the repeated 404/title block and error-swallowing catch are the main spots where a small refactor would pay off.

findings.issue: Every resolver's catch-all treats any API failure (network error, 500, timeout) as a missing resource, rendering 'Not found' and returning HTTP 404.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the rejection: emit a null/404 only for genuine not-found responses and surface an error state (or rethrow) otherwise.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but nothing in src imports it; the app uses native form controls directly.
findings.suggestion: Remove @angular/forms from dependencies to keep the install lean.

findings.issue: vitest, jsdom and tsconfig.spec.json are scaffolded for `ng test`, but the app contains zero test files.
findings.suggestion: Either write unit tests for the pure helpers (util.ts, resolver transforms) or trim the unused test scaffolding.

findings.issue: The title + RESPONSE_INIT 404 pattern is duplicated across five files (pokemon/move/ability/type resolvers and not-found-view).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared `notFound(titleService, responseInit)` helper next to NotFoundView so the pattern lives in one place.

findings.issue: Runtime config reaches the browser via a render-blocking /config.js script that sets a window.__API_BASE_URL__ global, read through an untyped globalThis cast (app/src/app/api.ts:19).
findings.suggestion: Proxy /api/v2 through the Express server so the browser uses same-origin relative URLs, removing the global and the blocking script; or at least serve the value as a typed meta tag.

findings.issue: withHttpTransferCacheOptions({}) is a no-op — provideClientHydration() already enables the HTTP transfer cache by default since Angular 20.
findings.suggestion: Drop the empty options call, or set the options you actually care about (e.g. includeRequestsWithAuthHeaders).

findings.issue: Request URLs are assembled by string concatenation and regex (also idFromUrl in util.ts:12).
findings.suggestion: Use URL/URLSearchParams for building request URLs; keep the regex only where the API genuinely hands back opaque URL strings.

findings.issue: Every search keystroke triggers router.navigate with queryParamsHandling merge, pushing a history entry per character typed.
findings.suggestion: Debounce the navigation (Angular 22 ships debounced()) or navigate with replaceUrl: true so Back isn't polluted by each keystroke.

summary: This is about as current as Angular gets: pinned to v22.2 and actually using v22's newest stable APIs (@Service, BootstrapContext, AngularNodeAppEngine with allowedHosts, RESPONSE_INIT, signal inputs, zoneless defaults) while avoiding everything v22 deprecated. Data access and typing are cleanly centralized, so framework or API churn would touch few files. The deductions are minor housekeeping: an unused @angular/forms dependency, empty test scaffolding, a copy-pasted 404/title block, and catch-alls that turn API outages into 'Not found'.

apis.replacement: Route resources (withRouterResources + resources route config) are developer preview in v22 and the router docs' recommended signal-era alternative, but not yet stable
AngularNodeAppEngine — correctly not used (deprecated since v22)
